ei.title: Chapter 0-QN31-34 2번: The Personal Nature of Transportation Debates
ei.subject: 올림포스9대변별유형

fullPassage: Everyone who drives, walks, or swipes a transit card in a city views herself as a transportation expert from the moment she walks out the front door. And how she views the street tracks pretty closely with how she gets around. That's why we find so many well-intentioned and civic-minded citizens arguing past one another. At neighborhood meetings in school auditoriums, and in back rooms at libraries and churches, local residents across the nation gather for often-contentious discussions about transportation proposals that would change a city's streets. And like all politics, all transportation is local and intensely personal. A transit project that could speed travel for tens of thousands of people can be stopped by objections to the loss of a few parking spaces or by the simple fear that the project won't work. It's not a challenge of the data or the traffic engineering or the planning. Public debates about streets are typically rooted in emotional assumptions about how a change will affect a person's commute, ability to park, belief about what is safe and what isn't, or the bottom line of a local business.

❌ ③ expert(전문가): 사람의 자격이지 이동 아님
✅ ④ commute(통근): 집과 직장 사이 규칙적 이동 — 정의 일치 ←정답
det.tip: commute = 통근(하다), 집과 직장을 오가는 규칙적 이동

questions.passage: That's why we find so many well-intentioned and civic-minded citizens arguing past one another. And like all politics, all transportation is local and __________ (intense) personal.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 'local and ___ personal'에서 형용사 personal을 수식하므로 부사 자리. intense(형용사) → intensely(부사). 'local and intensely personal' = 지역적이고 매우 개인적인
det.tip: intense(adj. 강렬한) → intensely(adv. 매우) → intensity(n. 강렬함)

questions.passage: It's not a challenge of the data or the traffic engineering or the planning. Public debates about streets are typically rooted in emotional __________ (assume) about how a change will affect a person's commute.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.analysis: 'rooted in emotional ___ about'에서 형용사 emotional의 수식을 받는 명사 자리이고 뒤에 복수 취급되므로 assume(동사) → assumptions(명사, 복수). 'emotional assumptions' = 감정적인 가정들

questions.passage: Everyone who drives, walks, or swipes a transit card in a city views herself as a transportation expert from the moment she walks out the front door. And how she views the street tracks pretty closely with how she gets around. That's why we find so many well-intentioned and civic-minded citizens arguing past one another. At neighborhood meetings in school auditoriums, and in back rooms at libraries and churches, local residents across the nation gather for often-contentious discussions about transportation proposals that would change a city's streets. And like all politics, all transportation is local and intensely personal. A transit project that could speed travel for __________ of people can be stopped by objections to the loss of a few parking spaces or by the simple fear that the project won't work. It's not a challenge of the data or the traffic engineering or the planning. Public debates about streets are typically rooted in emotional assumptions about how a change will affect a person's commute, ability to park, belief about what is safe and what isn't, or the bottom line of a local business.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 수만 명의 이동을 빠르게 할 수 있는 프로젝트
det.analysis:
❌ ① a small number(소수): 뒤에서 '몇 개의 주차 공간'이라는 소수와 대비되는 다수가 필요
❌ ② just a couple(단 두어 명): 다수를 강조하는 흐름과 반대
✅ ③ tens of thousands(수만 명): 소수의 반대 때문에 좌절되는 '수만 명'의 이동 — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ one or two(한두 명): 규모 대비 논지와 맞지 않음
